question.problem: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $80u+35v=\text{gcd}(80,35).$ What is the value of $u+v?$

current_example.problem: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $30u + 8v = \text{gcd}(30,8).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
current_example.worked_solution:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}30 & = & 8\cdot 3 & + & 6 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 8 & = & 6\cdot 1 & + & 2 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 6 & = & 2\cdot 3 & + & 0\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $\text{gcd}(30,8) =2.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, up to (and including) the equation where the greatest common divisor appeared as a remainder, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}6 & =30-8\cdot 3 \\ 2 & =8-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =8-6 \\  & =8-(30-8\cdot 3) \\  & =8\cdot 4-30 \\  & =30\cdot (-1)+8\cdot 4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $u=-1$ and $v=4.$

Finally, 

$$
u+v=(-1)+4=3.
$$
